meetingTitle: Q4 Sprint Planning & Architecture Modernization Sync
executiveSummary: The engineering team finalized the architectural approach for the Q4 database migration from monolithic Postgres to a distributed sharded setup. Key risks around read latency during peak hours were resolved by introducing a Redis Sentinel caching layer. Marcus and Elena aligned on a phased rollback mechanism to ensure 99.99% uptime during the transition scheduled for the first weekend of next month.

keyDecisions.decision: Adopt Redis Sentinel cluster for tier-1 session and hot-record caching.
keyDecisions.rationale: Reduces read queries on primary DB by an estimated 65% during flash traffic surges.

keyDecisions.decision: Execute schema migration using blue-green database deployment with dual-write replication.
keyDecisions.rationale: Eliminates customer downtime and provides immediate instant fallback if error rate exceeds 0.05%.

keyDecisions.decision: Postpone GraphQL federation v2 to Q1 to keep sprint scope focused exclusively on database stability.
keyDecisions.rationale: Prevents team burnout and isolates regression testing variables.

Create Grafana dashboard with alerting rules for replication lag > 500ms.
Update customer maintenance window disclosure and draft release changelog.
Sign off on AWS reserved instance allocation budget with finance.
Conduct load testing simulation with 50,000 concurrent virtual users.

unresolvedQuestions.question: What is the exact failover latency if the primary Redis node drops in AWS us-east-1?
unresolvedQuestions.context: Marcus will run chaos testing in staging on Thursday to verify whether reconnect takes under 3 seconds.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Will European GDPR compliance requirements affect the backup snapshot storage region?
unresolvedQuestions.context: Priya to verify with the data privacy officer before replication across regions is configured.

topics.summary: Marcus presented metrics from last Tuesday's spike where connection pool starvation caused 400ms p99 latency. The bottleneck was tied to unindexed join queries on tenant audit logs.

topics.topic: Redis Sentinel vs Redis Cluster Evaluation
topics.summary: Alex detailed why Sentinel is sufficient for current key counts (under 40GB working set) while avoiding the operational complexity of full cluster slot rebalancing.
Cutover planned for Sunday Dec 6 at 02:00 UTC. Dual-write will run in shadow mode for 72 hours prior to final traffic switch.
Elena confirmed two senior engineers will be dedicated full-time to regression testing, pausing non-critical UI features.

transcript.speaker: Priya Sharma
transcript.text: Good morning team. Today we're locking down the Q4 architecture plan for the database migration. Alex, why don't you kick off with where we landed on the caching layer?

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Thanks Priya. Looking at Tuesday's metrics, our biggest vulnerability during peak traffic is read pressure on the primary database instance. Marcus and I evaluated Redis Cluster versus Redis Sentinel.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Vance
transcript.text: Right. Our active cache footprint is only 32 Gigabytes. Cluster mode brings hash-slot rebalancing overhead that we simply don't need right now. With Sentinel, three nodes give us sub-second automatic failover with minimal operational friction.

transcript.speaker: Elena Rostova
transcript.text: From a product standpoint, what's our expected downtime during the actual cutover? Our enterprise enterprise SLAs guarantee 99.99% availability.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Zero scheduled downtime, Elena. We're running dual-write replication in shadow mode for 72 hours beforehand. When we flip the traffic router, if error rates spike above 0.05%, our proxy instantly switches back to the legacy Postgres cluster.

transcript.speaker: Priya Sharma
transcript.text: That gives me confidence. What about the GraphQL federation work we discussed last week?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Vance
transcript.text: I strongly suggest deferring GraphQL federation to Q1. Let's keep our sprint laser-focused on database stability and performance. Introducing schema stitching right now adds unnecessary risk variables.

transcript.speaker: Elena Rostova
transcript.text: I agree Marcus. I'll communicate to stakeholders that customer-facing GraphQL endpoints will land early January. Database resilience comes first.

transcript.speaker: Priya Sharma
transcript.text: Agreed. Let's wrap up with owners: Marcus on connection pooling benchmarks by Friday, Alex on Grafana alerts by Sunday, and I'll confirm AWS reserved pricing. Great work everyone.
